div.head: II As 11
div.ab: Be ðon ðe scyldgunge bæde æt ofslegenum. We cwædon be ðon ðe scyldgunga bæde æt ofslegenum ðeofe, þæt he eode ðreora sum, twegen fæderamagas ⁊ ðridda on medren, ⁊ ðone aþ sealde, þæt hi on heora mæge náne ðeofþe nysten, þæt he his feores wyrþe nære for ðæm gylt; ⁊ hio gan syþþan twelfa sum ⁊ gescylden hine, swa hit ær gecwæden wæs; ⁊ gif ðæs deadan magas ðeder cuman nyllan to ðæm andagan, gylde ælc CXX scill. ðe hit ær spræce.

Ond we cwædon: se ðe scyldunga bæde æt ofslagenum þeofe, ðæt he eode ðreora sum to, twegen on fæderanmaga ⁊ þridda on medren, ⁊ þone aþ syllen, ðæt hy on heora mæge nane þyfðe nysten, ðæt he his feores wyrðe nære for ðon gilte; ⁊ hy gán siððan XII sume ⁊ gescyldigen hine, swa hit ær gecweden wæs; ⁊ gif ðæs deadan mægas ðider cuman noldon to ðam andagan, gilde ælc ðe hit ær sprece CXX scll'.

[Be þam ðe scyldgung beodað æt ofslegenum þeof.] ⁊ we cwædon: se ðe scyld[gunga] bæde æt ofslegenum þeofe, þæt he eode þreora sum, twege[n fæde]ranmagas ⁊ þridda on medren, ⁊ þone að [sealde, þæt hie on] heora mæg nane þeofþe nysten, þæt he his [feores wyrð nære] for þam gylte; ⁊ [hie] gan siððan twelf[a sume ⁊ gescyldigen hine, swa] hit ær gecweden wæs; ⁊ gif þæs [deadan mægas þider cumm]an nellen to ðam [andagan, gylde ælc CXX scill' þe hit ær] sprece.

De illis qui culpam exigunt de fure occiso. Dictum est de illo qui culpam exigit de fure occiso, ut eat se tertio, et duo sint de cognatione (uel tribu) patris et tertius de cognatione matris, et iurent, quod in cognato suo nullum furtum sciebant (uel erat), pro quo uite sue reus esset; et eant alii cum XII et superiurent eum in immundiciam (contaminacionem) sicut ante dicitur. Quodsi parentes mortui nolint illuc uenire constituto (ire condicto) termino, emendet unusquisque CXX sol. qui hoc superloquebatur.

[Be ðon ðe scyldgunge bæde æt ofslegenum.] [Ld] Ond we cwædon: se ðe scyldunga bæde æt ofslagenum þeofe, ðæt he eode ðreora sum to, twegen on fæderanmaga ⁊ þridda on medren, ⁊ þone aþ syllen, ðæt hy on heora mæge nane þyfðe nysten, ðæt he his feores wyrðe nære for ðon gilte; ⁊ hy gán siððan XII sume ⁊ gescyldigen hine, swa hit ær gecweden wæs; ⁊ gif ðæs deadan mægas ðider cuman noldon to ðam andagan, gilde ælc ðe hit ær sprece CXX scll'.

And we have declared that he who demands redress for a slain thief shall go with three others, two [of the three] belonging to the father's kindred and one to the mother's, and they shall give an oath that they know of no theft committed by their kinsman, for perpetrating which he deserved to be put to death. The homicide shall go with the twelve others and charge the dead man with guilt in the manner already ordained. And if the kinsmen of the dead man will not come thither at the appointed day, each of those who have demanded redress shall pay 120 shillings.

(Von denen, die Schuldgeld fordern [dem, der Schuldgeld forderte Ld] für einen erschlagenen Dieb. So) Und wir bestimmten: wer (über den, welcher Ld) wegen eines erschlagenen Diebes [Wergeld-]schuld [vom Todtschläger] fordert, dass er selbdritt auftrete — zwei auf [Seite] der Vatersippe [des Erschlagenen] und der dritte auf der mütterlichen —, und sie sollen (er soll Ld So) folgenden Eid ablegen: ‘dass sie an ihrem [erschlagenen] Verwandten irgend einen Diebstahl, so dass er seines Lebens unwürdig gewesen sei wegen solcher Schuld, nicht kannten’. Und jene [Freunde des Todtschlägers] mögen danach selbzwölft auftreten und ihn als schuldig (über-)schwören, so wie es früher bestimmt worden ist. Und wenn die Verwandten des todten [Diebes] dorthin zum Termin nicht kommen wollen, zahle jeder, der zuvor das [Erschlagen des Diebes] einklagt(e Ld), 120 Schill. [dem König Strafe].

(Of those who demand guilt-payment [of him who demanded guilt-payment, Ld] for a slain thief. So) And we determined: whoever (concerning him who, Ld) demands [wergild-]payment [from the slayer] on account of a slain thief, that he is to come forward as one of three — two on [the side of] the father's kin [of the slain man] and the third on the mother's —, and they (he, Ld So) are to swear the following oath: ‘that they knew of no theft in their [slain] kinsman such that he would have been unworthy of his life on account of such guilt’. And those [friends of the slayer] may then come forward as one of twelve and swear him guilty, as was determined before. And if the kinsmen of the dead [thief] will not come there at the appointed day, let each who previously brought the charge [about the slaying of the thief] pay 120 shillings [as a fine to the king].
